metadata.description:
GUILLOTINE; Number 8; Jackson Heights; NY

by Wendy Eager



First published in 1981, Guillotine Zine continues today as an online 'zine (www.guillotinezine.com)


See also: More Guillotine (Issues 1, 2, 3); uploaded to the Internet Archive.


[Please Note: This scan of issue 8 of Guillotine is missing several pages.]




EDITORIAL


[Summary of the Original]


Response to Maximum Rocknroll's decision to publish a recent sensationalist and inflammatory letter portraying the New York scene as racist, promoting nazism and essentially serving as the headquarters of the National Front; false allegations that hinder NY bands from booking out-of-town shows.  The unprofessional decision to publish the letter reinforces the popular view that MRR has never really presented a favorable view of NY.  The publication of the opiniated, unsubstantiated allegations further reduces MRR's credibility.  The letter is more appropriate for publication in the National Enquirer.


Announcement that a new club called The Coventry has opened at Plaza 27 (Queensborough Plaza); features hardcore every Friday night.


Note to Javi Savage (Big City Fanzine): Ultraviolence [Wikiwand] did not appreciate the unauthorized use of one of their demo tapes.



INTERVIEWS


Agnostic Front (Wikipedia)


Jody Foster’s Army (JFA) (Wikipedia)


D.O.A. [link: early '80s interview: "D.O.A. Played"; Nihil Obstat #1]


The Psychos (Wikipedia)


Youth Brigade (Wikipedia)


Major Conflict (Discogs) with Dito Montiel (Wikipedia)


Iron Cross (Wikipedia)



LETTERS


A Reader Submits a Few Unsolicited Reviews / Cartoons / Photos:


-- the anarchic punk scene in NY sucks

[link: 'The Short, Tragic, and Instructive Life of Anarcho-Punk." (2020). Hampton Institute (HI). hamptonthink.org]


-- only CBGB regularly books hardcore; a few Brooklyn clubs closed after single gigs


-- participants of the clubs are partially responsible; (eg. in The V.I.P. Room the singer for Hellbent broke a water pipe)

[link: "NYC D-Beat History! Streaming: HELLBENT - NYC D-Beat Punk Pioneers." CVLT NATION. cvltnation.com]


-- at the Mad Club there were so many fights (mostly among girls) the owner pulled the plug early


-- hopefully the nonviolence at CBGB will last forever, and the price increases (now $5) will not


-- the reader's Review of N.Y.P.D. / Satan's Cheerleaders / Nihilistics; Venue:  My Father's Place; N.Y.P.D. (Long Island) played because Murphy's Law didn't show; Satan's Cheerleaders is the best, original new band with lyrics that employ intelligent use of figurative language and interesting musical findings in rhythm and tempo


-- Nihilistics [Interview 2020; No Echo] were taping a video that night, and were fast, tight, and not too drunk.  But they were boring; had to ask for applause and mention Atlantic's interest in the band.  The audience -- 90% of which did not know the meaning of 'Nihilishm,' fought off yawning.


-- the reader adds that he's been living in the U.S.A. for 4 years, welcomes questions about Russia and Russians, and praises democracy despite its inherent weak points


A Reader Submits a Poem Entitled "Guilt'


-- the poet was told by a mentor-of-sorts that the magazine might not find the poem 'hardcore enough'


-- the poet submitted the poem anyway, partially due to the absence of a 'hardcore material only' notice next to the fanzine's address


-- the poet's poem, 'Guilt,' is published in this issue

GUILLOTINE; Number 8; Jackson Heights; NY

by Wendy Eager



First published in 1981, Guillotine Zine continues today as an online 'zine (www.guillotinezine.com)


See also: More Guillotine (Issues 1, 2, 3); uploaded to the Internet Archive.


[Please Note: This scan of issue 8 of Guillotine is missing several pages.]




EDITORIAL


[Summary of the Original]


Response to Maximum Rocknroll's decision to publish a recent sensationalist and inflammatory letter portraying the New York scene as racist, promoting nazism and essentially serving as the headquarters of the National Front; false allegations that hinder NY bands from booking out-of-town shows.  The unprofessional decision to publish the letter reinforces the popular view that MRR has never really presented a favorable view of NY.  The publication of the opiniated, unsubstantiated allegations further reduces MRR's credibility.  The letter is more appropriate for publication in the National Enquirer.


Announcement that a new club called The Coventry has opened at Plaza 27 (Queensborough Plaza); features hardcore every Friday night.


Note to Javi Savage (Big City Fanzine): Ultraviolence [Wikiwand] did not appreciate the unauthorized use of one of their demo tapes.



INTERVIEWS


Agnostic Front (Wikipedia)

Iron Cross (Wikipedia)



LETTERS


A Reader Submits a Few Unsolicited Reviews / Cartoons / Photos:


-- the anarchic punk scene in NY sucks

[link: 'The Short, Tragic, and Instructive Life of Anarcho-Punk." (2020). Hampton Institute (HI). hamptonthink.org]


-- only CBGB regularly books hardcore; a few Brooklyn clubs closed after single gigs


-- participants of the clubs are partially responsible; (eg. in The V.I.P. Room the singer for Hellbent broke a water pipe)

[link: "NYC D-Beat History! Streaming: HELLBENT - NYC D-Beat Punk Pioneers." CVLT NATION. cvltnation.com]


-- at the Mad Club there were so many fights (mostly among girls) the owner pulled the plug early


-- hopefully the nonviolence at CBGB will last forever, and the price increases (now $5) will not


-- the reader's Review of N.Y.P.D. / Satan's Cheerleaders / Nihilistics; Venue:  My Father's Place; N.Y.P.D. (Long Island) played because Murphy's Law didn't show; Satan's Cheerleaders is the best, original new band with lyrics that employ intelligent use of figurative language and interesting musical findings in rhythm and tempo


-- Nihilistics [Interview 2020; No Echo] were taping a video that night, and were fast, tight, and not too drunk.  But they were boring; had to ask for applause and mention Atlantic's interest in the band.  The audience -- 90% of which did not know the meaning of 'Nihilishm,' fought off yawning.


-- the reader adds that he's been living in the U.S.A. for 4 years, welcomes questions about Russia and Russians, and praises democracy despite its inherent weak points


A Reader Submits a Poem Entitled "Guilt'


-- the poet was told by a mentor-of-sorts that the magazine might not find the poem 'hardcore enough'


-- the poet submitted the poem anyway, partially due to the absence of a 'hardcore material only' notice next to the fanzine's address


-- the poet's poem, 'Guilt,' is published in this issue
